back: Assets = Equity + Liabilities. Every transaction keeps the balance sheet balanced.
Net income = Income − Expenses. Expenses + Profit = Income. Profit goes to equity (net income for the year).
Equity = Assets − Liabilities = the company's book value. It is other financial resources, not repayable.
Balance sheet (position), income statement (performance), statement of cash flows (cash movements).
Net cash = cash and cash equivalents − bank overdrafts.
Change in cash + opening cash balance = closing cash balance.
Assets and expenses increase on the left (debit). Equity, liabilities and income increase on the right (credit).
Balance = |Σ debits − Σ credits|. Σ debits larger: debit balance. Σ credits larger: credit balance.
Income tax = taxable profit × tax rate. Taxable profit is not always equal to accounting profit.
Profit (loss) for the year = accounting profit − income tax. Tax payable is a liability until paid.
Profits kept in the company. Retained earnings are not cash.
Not an expense. Paid out of distributable profit (retained earnings + profit for the year > 0); a financing cash flow.
Credit sale creates trade receivables. Credit purchase creates trade payables. Cash moves later.
Operating expense for inventory used when a sale occurs. Sale gives revenue; the drawdown cuts inventory and adds cost of sales.
Record revenues and expenses when earned or incurred, not when cash moves.

front: Cost to company of an employee
back: Cost to the company = gross salary + employer's social security contributions.
Net salary = gross salary − employee's social security contributions.
Assets used for more than one year by the company (e.g. machinery, delivery trucks).
Rate = 100% / expected useful life. Useful life of 4 years gives 25%.
Gross carrying amount × rate × pro rata temporis. 24,000 × 25% × 9/12 = 4,500 for a machine used 9 months.
IFRS: depreciation for property, plant and equipment; amortization for intangibles (e.g. a patent).
Gross carrying amount − accumulated depreciation. 24,000 − 4,500 = 19,500 after the first year.
Share capital = number of shares × par value. 10,000 shares × 10 = 100,000.
Number of new shares × (issue price − par value). 2,000 × (15 − 10) = 10,000.
Equity / number of shares (book value per share), calculated from the balance sheet.
Annual installment = principal repayment + interest.
Interest = principal outstanding at beginning of year × rate (5% in the slides), paid 31 December.
Principal repaid = 50,000 / 5 = 10,000 a year. Interest falls each year, so installments fall.
Installment fixed (11,549). Principal repayment = installment − interest.
Recognized if carrying amount > recoverable amount. Loss = carrying amount − recoverable amount (e.g. 42,000 − 33,000 = 9,000).
Recognized under the prudence principle for a probable outflow from a past event (e.g. lawsuit, warranty), at the estimated amount.
Exclude the part relating to next year. 3,000 for 3 months starting Jan X3: remove 3,000 × 1/3 = 1,000 from X2 expenses.
Exclude revenue for next year. 12,000 with 3 of 12 months in X3: revenue X2 = 12,000 − 3,000 = 9,000.
Expense incurred but unpaid. Interest on 50,000 at 5% for 3 months: 50,000 × 5% × 3/12 = 625.
